profile.beat: Short-term options and swing trading education centered on US large-cap tech, AI semis and memory names plus SPY day trades, used to market a paid trading community (Wolves, via whop/Discord).
profile.style: Chart-only: every call is framed through his 8/21 EMA cross plus 'Break. Retest. Enter' setup at daily demand zones or key levels. Conviction is expressed through all-caps hype and after-the-fact option gain screenshots rather than position sizing or fundamentals. Sector ETF lists are used to point to leaders rather than to state discrete positions.
profile.cadence: Several posts a day: all-caps educational hooks, trade-recap brags, lifestyle/income posts, sales pitches for a 50% off summer sale, and short replies to followers. Recurring 'setup' template posts and weekend sector-scan lists.
profile.revisits: Yes, retrospectively: 2102477596693053651 quotes an earlier post to claim the MU/SNDK/DRAM/ARM bottom buy, and 2102561000377418204 reuses the same names as a study case. The SPY put trade is revisited in 2102827069361066204 and 2102936836599418919.
profile.caveats: Heavily promotional: the feed sells a paid community with income and lifestyle testimonials, and trade results are self-reported option gains shown after the fact with no verifiable entries or exits. Long ticker lists (e.g. the AI-cycle list in 2101744753419407396) are marketing-style watchlists, not demonstrated positions. Most trades are intraday options, so stances on names are short-lived.

narrative: Across the window the author pushes a single message: AI-cycle leaders, especially memory ($MU, $SNDK) and semis, are breaking out again and followers should not sit on the sidelines. On 2026-09-19 he flags memory, semis and hardware as the groups that led the last AI move and are breaking out again, and on 2026-09-20 publishes a broad 'retire early from the AI cycle' positioning list spanning compute, infrastructure, power, raw materials and physical AI. On 2026-09-21 he declares SPY, QQQ, AMD/INTC and MU/SNDK all breaking out. On 2026-09-22 and 2026-09-23 he claims credit for buying MU, SNDK, DRAM and ARM at daily demand when others were scared, presenting it as a repeatable bottom-buying model. Midweek the tone turns tactical: on 2026-09-23 he highlights an SPY put trade on a daily-low break and posts a short-side setup the next morning, then on 2026-09-24 flips to an SPY call trade on a break-and-retest. The directional AI/memory bullishness never changes; the SPY trades are intraday flips driven by his 8/21 EMA rules. Interleaved throughout is a sales push for the paid community's ending discount.
